newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Medium, long-term outlook excellent-Fernz.
newsitem.headline: Medium, long-term outlook excellent-Fernz.

text.p: New Zealand agricultural and industrial chemicals company Fernz Corporation said on Wednesday it considered its medium to long term prospects to be "excellent".
Fernz reported a net profit for the year to May 31 of NZ$46.81 million, up 7.5 percent on last year's $43.5 million.
Operating earnings before interest and taxation rose by 20.5 percent to $75.3 million, in line with forecast.
"The result has been recorded in a year in which a great deal has been accomplished in terms of financial structuring and strategic focusing of the company for the future," Fernz said in a statement.

Over the 12 month period, the crop protection business of Akzo Nobel in the Netherlands was acquired and incorporated into the group's agricultural chemical operations, strengthening the company's position in the international phenoxy herbicide market.

The chemical trading business of the company had been significantly enhanced with the acquisition of Laporte Group Australia, Fidene Consolidated and the remaining equity in Pacific Raw Materials, and Agrow Australia, which was not previously owned.

In addition an important 45.13 percent strategic equity investment was made in the French publicly listed agricultural and industrial chemical company CFPI, and negotiations were completed on June 1 for sale of Fernz' fertiliser manufacturing and marketing operations at Whangarei and New Plymouth.

"The new businesses have been incorporated into the company's results for the year ended May 31, except that in the case of the CFPI investment, only 26 percent of its net profitability has been equity accounted and all holding costs have been expenses," Fernz said. It said the balance of the current equity holding was not acquired until the end of May.
Group turnover in the year increased by 30.2 percent to $830.5 million. Of this figure, 27 percent was generated in New Zealand, 48 percent in Australia and 25 percent in other international markets.
Fernz said its investment in industrial chemicals during the year was reflected in the 227 percent increase in sales to $255 million.
"In the space of 12 months industrial chemicals have risen from 12 percent to 31 percent of turnover, and now represent a major sector of our international business," Fernz said.
Fertiliser sales, while down 12 percent on last year, were in line with forecast at $92.7 million.
"Directors consider the medium to long term prospects for the company remain excellent," Fernz said.
